method: Per request, from the rollout's token_count records: uncached input = input - cached input; output includes reasoning. A request whose input exceeds 272K tokens is priced at the long-context rates; all others at the short-context rates. No cache writes were reported.

records.note: The largest single request carried 308,123 input tokens. The pricing page does not say whether the long-context rate applies per request or to a whole session; per request is used here. Failed or retried transport attempts during the network outages are not in the usage records.

records.method: Session totals from the modelUsage field of the stream-json result line (Claude Code's own count, main thread and helper agents together). Cache writes split by duration from the per-message usage in the log: every main-thread write was a 1-hour write, every helper-agent write a 5-minute write. Anthropic lists no long-context surcharge for Sonnet 5.5, so one rate per token category applies.
records.note: modelUsage has 16,624 more cache-write tokens than the per-message log; they are priced at the 5-minute rate with the other helper writes, and with that split the sum reproduces Claude Code's total_cost_usd exactly. Thinking tokens are counted inside outputTokens. Requests by thread, from the per-message usage in the log: 54 main thread, 563 across the five helper agents. Their logged cache reads (6,385,214 main, 180,602,315 helpers) sum to 1.2% less than modelUsage; the totals use modelUsage. The run used a Claude subscription, so this is an estimate at list price, not a cash charge. The v1 card showed $5.97 for a single-thread run.
